title: Felix and the Protocol
premise: Mara Thackeray has spent eleven years tending a derelict beacon at the edge of contested space, hiding among the cryo-pods of passengers who never woke — backups of people the war erased. When a ghost ship docks carrying a manifest with his dead sister's name and a sealed diplomatic message, Mara learns the beacon he maintains is actually a dead-drop for peace negotiations between the Concord and the Meridian Compact. Hunted by Concord intelligence officer Sefa Idris, who slowly becomes his reluctant ally and something more, Mara must choose between destroying the message to keep his found family of station misfits safe, or delivering it and exposing everyone he loves. He delivers it: the truth ends the war, but only after the station burns, Sefa defects, and Mara finally lets the backups in the hold be mourned instead of hidden.
about_author: Quentin Okonkwo is a former maritime radio operator from Lagos who now writes science fiction about lonely signals and the people who answer them. His work has appeared in several genre anthologies, and 'Felix and the Protocol' is his second novel.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. We meet him mid-routine: calibrating the ancient beacon, logging the cryo-hold, sharing synthetic tea with Dex the engineer and Wren the stowaway botanist — his accidental family. A ship that matches no registry appears on approach. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath comfortable routine; invisibility as both armor and prison.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Never-Flown
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The ghost ship docks empty except for one sealed courier case and a manifest listing 'A. Thackeray' — his sister, dead nine years. He opens the case against every instinct and finds an encrypted protocol keyed to the beacon itself. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by hope; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. While Mara obsesses over the case, Wren discovers the cryo-pods are drawing power again — someone or something is waking them. She keeps it from Mara to protect him. Emotional beat: love expressed as concealment; the first fracture in the family's honesty.

chapters.title: Sefa Idris Arrives
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A Concord intelligence cutter intercepts the station. Sefa Idris boards under a trade-inspection pretext, hunting the missing protocol. Her interrogation of Mara is a duel of omissions. Emotional beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's loneliness across an adversarial table.

chapters.title: Dead-Drop
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Decoding fragments, Mara learns the beacon was built by his sister as a neutral channel for peace talks — and that the 'backups' are witnesses to a Concord atrocity the war depends on burying. Sefa catches him mid-decryption and doesn't report it. Emotional beat: the price of survival revealed as complicity; trust offered against duty.

chapters.title: Waking the Witnesses
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. The pods open. The revived witnesses are confused, fragile, furious — including a woman wearing A. Thackeray's face: not Mara's sister, but her backup, carrying the final key in memory. Emotional beat: found family stretched to include the impossible; joy shadowed by terror of what waking them means.

chapters.title: Orders of Precedence
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Concord command orders Sefa to sterilize the station and all witnesses. She stalls, falsifies reports, and quietly warns Mara — burning her career in real time. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit; she chooses the man over the mission before either will say it aloud.

chapters.title: The Station Burns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, interwoven. A Concord strike team arrives early. Dex holds the docking ring, Wren shepherds the witnesses to the ghost ship, and the backup-sister unlocks the full protocol as the beacon tower takes fire. Emotional beat: sacrifice without hesitation; the invisible station finally visible in flames.

chapters.title: Deliver the Message
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Aboard the fleeing ghost ship, Mara must broadcast the protocol on the open band — ending the war or igniting a final purge, no way to know which. With Sefa's hand on his shoulder, he transmits. Emotional beat: climax as surrender of control; choosing truth over safety at the last possible second.

chapters.title: Felix
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. The truth lands: cease-fire signed, atrocities acknowledged, the witnesses named publicly. On a rebuilt station renamed Felix — his sister's word for 'lucky' — Mara buries the empty pods properly, and stays, no longer hiding. Emotional beat: mourning completed, family redefined, love allowed to remain.
